note: HOST COST of the simulator, as opposed to the in-game results in bn1.json.
The unit is `vhPerWallMinute` -- virtual hours of game bought per real
minute of waiting. It improves UPWARD. Everything else the harness reports
is virtual time and says nothing about how long a run takes to sit through.
TWO KINDS OF ENTRY, and mixing them up will mislead you.
A FIXED-HORIZON entry (`horizonHours`) runs a bounded amount of game and
measures how long that took. Identical work on both sides, so it is the
A/B metric: this is the number an optimisation has to move, and the one to
regress against.
A WALL-BUDGET entry (`wallBudget`) runs for a fixed real time and measures
how far into the game it got. It is a diagnostic, NOT an A/B: because cost
grows with run length, a faster simulator reaches the expensive late state
sooner and can end the window at the same virtual hour as a slower one.
Making the simulator 1.45x faster per unit of work moved this entry by
-2%. That is not a contradiction; it is the decay problem stated in one
number.
RULES.
1. Only move a number from a run you actually observed, and record the
machine: these are wall-clock measurements, so they are comparable
only against other measurements on the same hardware. A 5% gap is
noise; a 2x gap is a finding.
2. `decayPct` compares the mean per-interval throughput of the FIRST HALF
of a window's samples against the SECOND HALF -- not the first sample
against the last, which is the two least reliable readings (JIT warm-up,
and a partial tail). Strongly negative means cost grows with run length,
which is a different bug from `vhPerWallMinute` simply being low, and
the one this simulator has historically actually had (see
spec/simulator.md, 'Run-length pathologies').
3. A budgeted run never reaches its goal. These entries are diagnostics
and are never route evidence.
ID CHANGE (2026-08-29). `bn1-full` is now the route leg `leg-bn1.1` -- the
full-node benchmarks merged into the leg naming. The entrance is unchanged
(BN1 holding SF4.3), so these throughput numbers carry across; older notes
below still name the profile as it was when they were recorded.
HOW TO RE-MEASURE.
bun run sim -- --profile leg-bn1.1 --seed 1 --horizon 1h --compact --perf --cost
bun run sim -- --profile leg-bn1.1 --seed 1 --compact --perf --wall-budget 2m --cost
bun run sim:profile --cpu-prof --wall-budget 2m   # where the time goes
Same seed, same settings, an otherwise idle machine. Take the median of three.

Against a76d187b on the same machine: 10.8s / 5.57 vh/min before, 8.5s / 7.10 after (1.27x throughput). Full telemetry is byte-identical for bn1-full seed 1 at 1h, bn1-full seed 2 at 45m, bn1-speedrun seed 1 at 1h, and bn1-progression seed 1 at 30m.

leg-bn1.1.note: THE PROBLEM REMAINS. The factions pass improves identical early work and buys 6.03 virtual hours in this diagnostic window, but the first half still collapses from 5.29 to 0.72 vh/min in the second (-86%). A faster simulator reaches the expensive late state sooner; this endpoint is not the A/B metric.

The run-length decay is untouched and remains the open lead.
